title: Personal narrative: telling a true story in order
summary: Students plan a true story on a five-finger Story Hand, rehearse it aloud with a partner and write it with transition words, feeling words and one line of dialogue.

standard.text: Write narratives to develop real or imagined experiences or events using effective technique, descriptive details, and clear event sequences.

discourse: Tell one small, true moment from beginning to end in time order, instead of listing everything that happened in a day.
Show how the writer felt or what they thought at an important point, not only what they did.
Close the story with an ending that tells how it turned out or what the writer learned.
sentence: Past-tense verbs, including common irregular forms: went, saw, felt, made, ran, said, took.
Time clauses that join two events: When I opened the door, I saw ...; After we ate, we ...
Dialogue punctuated with quotation marks and a speaker tag: "Look out!" my brother shouted.
word: Transition words that move time forward: first, next, then, after that, suddenly, finally.
Feeling words beyond happy and sad: nervous, proud, excited, surprised, disappointed, relieved.
Sensory details: what the writer saw, heard, smelled, tasted or touched.

contentObjective: Students will plan and write a personal narrative about one true moment with a clear beginning, middle and end, descriptive details and an ending.
languageObjective: Students will narrate a true experience orally and in writing using past-tense verbs, at least three transition words (first, then, suddenly, finally) and one feeling word.

L3-4: At the end, ___, and I felt ___.
L5-6: My heart ___ when ___, and I thought, "___."
The ___ smelled like ___, which reminded me of ___.
"___," ___ said, and that is when I realized ___.

vocabulary.definition: a story that tells what happened, in order
the order in which events happen
a small piece of information that helps the reader picture the story
vocabulary.morphology: de- + Old French tailler, 'to cut': first meant a small piece cut off

vocabulary.definition: the exact words people say in a story, shown inside quotation marks
a word that tells the reader when something happened, such as first, next or finally
vocabulary.morphology: trans- 'across' + Latin ire 'to go': words that carry you across time

vocabulary.definition: a person or animal in a story; in a true story, the writer is a character too
an emotion, such as nervous, proud or excited

vocabulary.morphology: sudden + -ly (the -ly ending tells how something happened)

activity.title: Story Hand: Plan, Say, Write
steps: Model with a short true story of your own, for example: 'First, my aunt handed me a bowl of dough. Then I tried to roll it flat, but it kept sticking. Suddenly, she laughed and sprinkled flour on my nose. Finally, I made my first round, warm bread, and I felt proud.' Students listen for and count the transition words on their fingers.
Trace a hand on paper. Label the fingers: who and where, first, then, suddenly (the big moment), finally. Write the feeling word in the palm.

Students choose one small true moment: cooking with a family member, a first day somewhere new, a game, a celebration, a pet, a trip, learning to do something. They sketch or write two or three words on each finger.
Partners take turns telling their story aloud, touching each finger as they go. The listener asks one question: 'What did you see?' or 'How did you feel?' The teller adds that detail.
Students write their story, one or two sentences per finger, using the frames for their band. Challenge writers add one line of dialogue with quotation marks.
Partners reread each other's stories and underline every transition word and circle the feeling word. Two volunteers share aloud.

warmup: Picture Sequence: sketch three simple pictures on the board out of order (for example, a bare pot of soil, a small sprout, a flowering plant). Partners decide the order, then retell it aloud with First, Next, Finally and one past-tense verb per sentence. Repeat with a second set (packing a backpack, riding the bus, arriving at school) if time allows.
